records.correct_answer_text: Compute zone- and hour-level trip counts, pickup surges near transit hubs, and changes in trip distance/duration, then align them with outside records of transit service reductions/disruptions and typical ridership patterns.
records.incorrect_candidate: Aggregate weekly unique driver IDs per borough and align this with quarterly employment statistics for the transportation sector from the Bureau of Labor Statistics to infer substitution behavior.
records.Explanation: By aligning hourly TLC trip metrics with external schedules and incident logs of transit service cuts, you can see whether increases in taxi/FHV demand coincide with reduced transit availability, consistent with a substitution effect.
